_meta: Several tool calls issued together that finish in a different order than they were issued, used to show why a harness must match each tool RESULT back to its call by the call's id, not by the position/order in which results arrive -- or out-of-order completion pairs the wrong result with the wrong call and the model reasons on scrambled data. When a model emits multiple tool calls in one turn, a good harness runs them in parallel for speed. Parallel calls finish in an order determined by how long each takes, which has nothing to do with the order they were issued -- a fast lookup returns before a slow one issued earlier. The harness must then hand the results back to the model paired with the calls. The trap is pairing by arrival: taking the results in the order they completed and assigning them to the calls in the order they were issued, slot by slot. Because the two orders differ, every result can land on the wrong call -- the model is told the weather lookup returned a stock price, the stock lookup returned the time, and so on -- and it then reasons on data attributed to the wrong question, silently. The fix is to carry a unique id on each call (the tool_call_id in modern tool-calling APIs) and match each result to its call by that id, so completion order is irrelevant. calls lists each tool call with its id, the result it will return, and how long it takes (dur), issued in list order. calls is the fixture; the completion order, the naive position-based pairing, the correct id-based pairing, and the mismatches are computed.
